expert: J.A - creator and lead developer of UMBRAL (game design, bosses and the in-game ML)
method: Structured interview: the results of Phase 4 were explained in plain language and the expert answered four questions (answers recorded verbatim, in Spanish, and translated).
data_shown: First run of the pipeline (SIMULATED players while the real log fills up); to be repeated with the REAL data run.

answers.question: With ~50% accuracy (in-game model ~53%, new hybrid ~55%, majority class 37%), is the next-action prediction useful in practice for the bosses?
answers.answer_es: Sí, se nota en la pelea
answers.answer_en: Yes, it shows in the fight: at ~50% the boss can already feint or wait for your dodge sometimes, and it feels like it knows you.

answers.question: Which model would you put in the game for the next action?
answers.answer_es: El que gane en los datos
answers.answer_en: The one that wins on the data (best result with the real plays), even if it is heavier.

answers.question: Who is responsible for monitoring?
answers.answer_es: J.A modelo, J.P juego, J.Q web
answers.answer_en: J.A: model and data. J.P: integration in the game. J.Q: website and reports.

answers.question: What risks do you see in bosses using this?
answers.answer_es: Que se sienta injusto; demasiado difícil
answers.answer_en: That it feels unfair (the boss 'reads your mind') and that it becomes too hard for players who repeat patterns.

consequences: Selection criterion kept as fixed in Phase 1: best validation score wins (no extra weight to simplicity).

Fairness controls kept/added: bosses only use a prediction above a reliability threshold, never more than 60% of the time (guardian.gd caps the wait-for-dodge at 60%), and the boss telegraph still always happens.
Difficulty risk: accuracy and hit rate are monitored per difficulty (Phase 4 segments, Phase 6 indicators); Story mode and Easy keep adaptive level capped (adapt_level never rises in Story mode).
